Mix in the chopped onion, ground ginger, cayenne pepper, and salt thoroughly
Shape the mixture into small balls, rings, or flat sticks
Heat the reserved groundnut oil (or vegetable oil) in a deep pot until hot
Fry the shaped kuli kuli in batches until golden brown and crisp, turning frequently to prevent burning
Drain on paper towels and allow to cool completely before storing in an airtight container

title: Kilishi
ingredients: 1 tbsp ground cloves or suya spice blend
instructions: Slice the beef into very thin, wide sheets and lay them out to dry slightly under the sun or on a rack
Mix the roasted groundnut powder with ground chili pepper, ginger, cloves, and salt, adding a little water to form a thick paste
Coat both sides of the thin beef sheets generously with the spice paste
Return the coated meat to the drying rack and sun-dry or use a low oven until fully dehydrated
Lightly roast or grill the dried, spiced meat over an open flame briefly to finish and enhance flavor
Allow to cool completely before storing in an airtight container or serving as a snack

title: Plantain Chips
instructions: Peel the unripe plantains and slice them thinly, either lengthwise or into rounds
Soak the slices briefly in salted water if desired to season and prevent excess browning
Pat the plantain slices dry with a clean towel
Heat the vegetable oil in a deep pot until hot
Fry the plantain slices in batches, stirring occasionally, until golden and crisp
Drain on paper towels and sprinkle with a little extra salt while still warm
Allow to cool before storing in an airtight container

title: Bole (Roasted Plantain)
ingredients: 200 g fresh fish (such as croaker), cleaned
instructions: Wash the ripe plantains and slit the skin slightly along the length without fully peeling
Season the cleaned fish with sliced onion, sliced chili pepper, and a pinch of salt
Prepare a charcoal grill or open flame and allow it to reach a steady medium heat
Place the plantains and seasoned fish directly on the grill, turning occasionally to cook evenly on all sides
Baste the plantains and fish lightly with palm oil as they roast to add flavor and sheen
Roast the plantains for about 20-25 minutes until the skin is charred and the flesh is soft, and grill the fish until cooked through and lightly crisp
Peel the plantains and serve hot alongside the grilled fish

title: Nkwobi
ingredients: 1 kg cow foot, cleaned and cut into chunks
instructions: Boil the cow foot with a seasoning cube and salt until very tender, then drain and set aside
Heat the palm oil gently in a pot and whisk in the dissolved potash water until the oil thickens into a paste
Stir in the blended chili peppers and ground crayfish, mixing thoroughly into the thickened oil
Add the boiled cow foot to the spiced palm oil paste and toss until well coated
Transfer to a serving bowl and garnish with sliced onions and utazi leaves
Serve immediately as a communal snack, traditionally eaten with the hands

title: Isi Ewu
ingredients: 1 whole goat head, cleaned and cut into pieces
instructions: Singe and clean the goat head thoroughly, then cut into manageable pieces
Boil the goat head with a seasoning cube and salt until tender, then set the pieces aside and reserve some stock
Heat the palm oil in a pot and whisk in the dissolved potash water until it thickens into a smooth paste
Stir in the blended chili peppers and ground crayfish into the thickened palm oil paste
Add the boiled goat head pieces to the spiced paste, tossing to coat evenly, using a little reserved stock if needed
Garnish with sliced onions and utazi leaves before serving
Serve hot as a delicacy, typically shared and eaten with the hands

title: Gizdodo
ingredients: 500 g chicken gizzards, cleaned and boiled
instructions: Boil the cleaned gizzards with a little onion, seasoning cube, and salt until tender, then slice into bite-sized pieces
Fry the diced plantains in vegetable oil until golden on the edges, then remove and set aside
In the same pan, saute the chopped onion until fragrant
Add the chopped tomatoes, bell peppers, and blended chili peppers, frying until softened
Stir in the boiled gizzard pieces and cook for a few minutes to absorb the flavors
Fold in the fried plantains and toss gently to combine
Season with salt to taste and serve warm as a snack or side dish

title: Miyan Taushe
ingredients: 2 cups black-eyed peas or pumpkin, as base
instructions: Season and boil the assorted meat with onion, a seasoning cube, and salt until tender, keeping the stock
Boil the black-eyed peas or pumpkin until soft, then mash or blend into a smooth puree
Heat the vegetable oil in a pot and fry the chopped onion until translucent
Add the blended tomatoes and chili peppers, frying until the sauce thickens and the raw taste cooks off
Stir in the mashed pea or pumpkin puree along with the reserved meat stock
Add the boiled meat and ground crayfish, then simmer for 15 minutes until well combined and rich red in color
Season to taste and serve with tuwo or rice

title: Obe Ata (stew)
instructions: Season the chicken with one chopped onion, a seasoning cube, and salt, then boil until tender; reserve the stock
Heat the palm oil in a pot and fry the remaining chopped onion until fragrant
Add the blended tomatoes, tomato paste, and chili peppers, frying steadily until the sauce reduces and the oil rises to the top
Stir in the reserved chicken stock and remaining seasoning cube, then simmer for 10 minutes
Add the cooked chicken pieces to the sauce and simmer for another 10-15 minutes to absorb the flavors
Adjust salt to taste and serve hot with rice or any swallow

title: Pounded Yam
ingredients: 1 large yam tuber (about 1.5 kg), peeled and cubed
1/2 cup extra water for pounding, as needed
1 bowl clean water for wetting hands during pounding
instructions: Peel the yam and cut into evenly sized chunks
Place the yam chunks in a pot with water and boil until very soft and easily pierced with a fork
Drain the yam thoroughly, reserving a little of the cooking water
Transfer the boiled yam to a mortar or use an electric pounder, and pound continuously while folding the mass
Add small splashes of the reserved water as needed to achieve a smooth, stretchy, lump-free consistency
Shape the pounded yam into smooth mounds using wet hands or a spatula
Serve hot immediately alongside any Nigerian soup such as egusi or ogbono

title: Amala and Ewedu Soup
instructions: For the amala, gradually sprinkle the yam flour into boiling water while stirring vigorously to avoid lumps
Continue stirring and cooking the mixture over low heat until it forms a smooth, stretchy, dark brown dough
Mold the amala into smooth balls and set aside
For the ewedu, boil the chopped jute leaves until soft, then blend briefly and whisk vigorously to create a light, draw-y texture
Season and boil the assorted meat and fish separately with onion, seasoning cubes, and salt
Stir the boiled meat, fish, and locust beans into the whisked ewedu and simmer for a few minutes
Serve the amala hot alongside the ewedu soup

title: Semovita
ingredients: 1/2 cup extra water, as needed for consistency
1 bowl clean water for shaping servings
instructions: Bring the water to a boil in a heavy-bottomed pot
Gradually sprinkle in the semolina flour while stirring continuously to prevent lumps from forming
Reduce the heat to low and keep stirring and turning the mixture with a wooden spoon or turning stick
Cook, folding the dough over itself, until it becomes smooth, firm, and stretchy
Cover and let it steam briefly on very low heat for a couple of minutes to finish cooking through
Mold into smooth rounded servings using a spoon or wet hands
Serve hot with any Nigerian soup such as egusi, okra, or edikang ikong

title: Abacha
ingredients: 3 cups African salad (dried shredded cassava, abacha)
1/3 cup palm oil (potash-treated ncha ncha oil)
instructions: Soak the dried shredded cassava (abacha) in warm water for about 10-15 minutes until softened, then drain well
Warm the palm oil gently with a little potash water until it thickens slightly into a smooth paste
Toss the softened abacha with the thickened palm oil until every strand is evenly coated
Add the ground crayfish, sliced onion, chopped chili peppers, and seasoning cube, mixing thoroughly
Flake in the dried or smoked fish and toss gently to combine
Garnish with sliced utazi leaves just before serving
Serve at room temperature as a salad or light snack

title: Chicken Tagine with Preserved Lemon and Olives
ingredients: 1 whole chicken (about 3.5 lbs), cut into 8 pieces
instructions: Heat olive oil in a tagine or heavy pot over medium heat and add the sliced onions, cooking until softened.
Add garlic, ginger, turmeric, saffron, and the cinnamon stick, stirring until fragrant.
Place the chicken pieces on top of the onions, season with salt and pepper, and add half the chopped cilantro.
Pour in the water or stock, cover, and simmer gently for 45 minutes, turning the chicken occasionally.
Add the preserved lemon quarters and olives, then continue cooking uncovered for 15-20 minutes until the sauce thickens and chicken is tender.
Adjust seasoning, sprinkle with remaining cilantro, and serve hot directly from the tagine with bread.

title: Couscous with Seven Vegetables
ingredients: 1 lb lamb or beef, cut into chunks
instructions: In the bottom of a couscoussier, brown the meat and onion in olive oil, then add ginger, turmeric, and salt.
Add water to cover, add the soaked chickpeas, and simmer for 45 minutes.
Add the carrots and turnips and continue cooking for 15 minutes, then add pumpkin, cabbage, and tomatoes and cook until vegetables are tender.
Meanwhile, steam the couscous over the simmering stew in the couscoussier's top basket, fluffing and moistening with water three times over about an hour.
Toss the finished couscous with butter and a bit of the cooking broth until light and fluffy.
Mound the couscous on a large platter, arrange the meat and vegetables on top, and moisten with extra broth before serving.

title: Harira Soup
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot and brown the meat with onion and celery.
Add ginger, turmeric, salt, pepper, tomato paste, and grated tomatoes, and cook for a few minutes.
Add the soaked chickpeas and enough water to cover generously, then simmer covered for about 1 hour until meat is tender.
Add the lentils and continue simmering for 20-30 minutes until lentils are soft.
Whisk the flour with water to make a smooth slurry (tadouira) and stir it gradually into the soup to thicken.
Simmer another 10 minutes, stir in cilantro and parsley, and serve hot with lemon wedges and dates.

title: Pastilla
ingredients: 1 cup blanched almonds, toasted and crushed
1 tsp ground cinnamon, plus more for dusting
1/4 cup powdered sugar, plus more for dusting
instructions: Simmer the poultry with onion, saffron, ginger, cilantro, salt, and water until fully cooked and tender, then remove meat and shred it, reserving the broth.
Reduce the reserved broth, then whisk in the beaten eggs over low heat, stirring until they scramble into a thick, moist mixture.
Mix the toasted crushed almonds with powdered sugar and a pinch of cinnamon to make the almond filling.
Layer buttered warqa sheets in a round baking dish, spreading the almond mixture, then the shredded meat, then the egg mixture in distinct layers, folding sheets over to enclose.
Brush the top with more melted butter and bake at 375°F until golden and crisp, about 25-30 minutes.
Dust the top with powdered sugar and cinnamon in a decorative pattern before serving warm.

title: Zaalouk
instructions: Peel the eggplants and cut into chunks, then steam or boil until very soft.
Heat olive oil in a pan and sauté the garlic briefly until fragrant.
Add the chopped tomatoes, cumin, paprika, cayenne, and salt, and cook until the tomatoes break down into a sauce.
Mash the cooked eggplant and add it to the pan, stirring to combine with the tomato mixture.
Simmer uncovered, mashing occasionally, until the mixture is thick and jam-like, about 15-20 minutes.
Stir in lemon juice and fresh cilantro, then let cool slightly and serve at room temperature with bread.

title: Kefta Tagine
instructions: Combine the ground meat with grated onion, half the parsley and cilantro, garlic, cumin, paprika, cinnamon, and salt, then shape into small meatballs.
Heat olive oil in a tagine or wide pan and sauté the sliced onion until softened.
Add the grated tomatoes and simmer for 10 minutes to form a sauce, seasoning with salt and pepper.
Gently place the kefta meatballs into the simmering tomato sauce, cover, and cook for about 15-20 minutes, turning carefully once.
Crack the eggs directly into the sauce between the meatballs and cover until the eggs are just set.
Sprinkle with the remaining parsley and cilantro and serve directly from the tagine with bread.

title: Koshari
ingredients: 1 tsp dried chili flakes or chili vinegar
instructions: Cook the brown lentils in water until tender, then drain and set aside.
Cook the rice separately in salted water until fluffy, and boil the macaroni until al dente.
Make the tomato sauce by sautéing garlic in a little oil, adding tomato sauce, cumin, salt, and pepper, and simmering for 10 minutes.
In a small pan, combine vinegar with fried garlic and chili flakes to make the sharp dakka sauce.
Deep fry thinly sliced onions in vegetable oil until crisp and golden, then drain on paper towels.
Layer the rice, lentils, and macaroni in a serving dish, top generously with tomato sauce and crispy onions, and serve the vinegar-garlic sauce on the side.

title: Molokhia
ingredients: 1 lb fresh or frozen molokhia leaves, finely chopped
instructions: Simmer the chicken in water with salt until fully cooked and tender, then remove the meat and strain and reserve the broth.
Bring the reserved chicken broth to a simmer in a pot and add the finely chopped molokhia leaves.
Cook the molokhia gently, stirring frequently, for about 15-20 minutes until slightly thickened; avoid vigorous boiling to keep it from becoming stringy.
In a separate small pan, melt ghee and fry the minced garlic with coriander and dried mint until fragrant, forming the takleya.
Stir the garlic-herb takleya into the molokhia pot and simmer for a few more minutes, adjusting seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve the molokhia hot over white rice, with the cooked chicken pieces on the side.

title: Ful Medames
ingredients: 2 cups dried fava beans, soaked overnight
instructions: Drain the soaked fava beans and place them in a large pot with fresh water to cover generously.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer slowly, covered, for 2-3 hours until the beans are very soft, adding water as needed.
Once tender, mash some of the beans lightly with a fork while leaving others whole, keeping some of the cooking liquid for a creamy consistency.
Stir in crushed garlic, olive oil, lemon juice, cumin, and salt, mixing well.
Transfer to serving bowls and top with chopped tomatoes, onion, and parsley.
Serve warm with hard-boiled eggs on the side and flatbread for scooping.

title: Mahshi (Stuffed Vegetables)
ingredients: 8 small zucchini or bell peppers, hollowed
instructions: Hollow out the zucchini or peppers using a corer, reserving the shells and discarding or saving the pulp.
Mix the rice with chopped tomatoes, parsley, dill, tomato paste, olive oil, cumin, mint, and salt to make the stuffing.
Loosely stuff each vegetable shell about three-quarters full with the rice mixture to allow room for expansion.
Arrange the stuffed vegetables snugly in a pot, tucking sliced garlic between them.
Pour tomato juice or broth over the vegetables until mostly covered, place a plate on top to hold them down, and cover the pot.
Simmer gently for 45 minutes to 1 hour until the rice is fully cooked and vegetables are tender, then serve warm.

title: Kofta
instructions: Combine the ground meat with grated onion, garlic, parsley, cumin, coriander, allspice, cinnamon, salt, and pepper in a large bowl.
Knead the mixture thoroughly until well combined and slightly sticky.
Shape the mixture into elongated logs around skewers or into small oval patties.
Brush lightly with olive oil and grill or broil over high heat, turning occasionally, until browned and cooked through, about 8-10 minutes.
Rest briefly, then serve hot with flatbread, grilled tomatoes, and tahini or salad.

title: Couscous Tunisien
instructions: Brown the lamb chunks with chopped onion in olive oil in the bottom of a couscoussier.
Stir in tomato paste, harissa, and caraway seeds, cooking briefly until fragrant.
Add water or broth and the soaked chickpeas, then simmer covered for about 45 minutes.
Add the carrots and pumpkin and continue cooking until the meat and vegetables are tender.
While the stew simmers, steam the couscous in the top basket of the couscoussier, fluffing with a little water and oil two to three times over about 45 minutes.
Spread the couscous on a platter, ladle the spicy lamb and vegetable stew and broth over the top, and serve hot.

title: Brik
ingredients: 4 sheets malsouka or brik pastry (or thin phyllo)
1 cup canned tuna, drained and flaked
instructions: Mix the flaked tuna with chopped onion, parsley, capers, mashed potato if using, salt, and pepper.
Lay a sheet of malsouka flat and place a portion of the tuna mixture on one half, making a small well in the center.
Crack an egg into the well on top of the tuna filling.
Quickly fold the pastry over into a half-moon or triangle shape, sealing the edges firmly to prevent the egg from leaking.
Heat vegetable oil in a skillet and carefully slide in the brik, frying quickly on each side for about 1-2 minutes until golden and crisp while the egg yolk stays soft.
Drain briefly on paper towels and serve immediately with lemon wedges.

title: Lablabi
ingredients: 2 cups cooked chickpeas, with some cooking liquid reserved
4 cups chickpea cooking broth or water
4 slices day-old bread, torn into pieces
instructions: Heat the chickpea broth in a pot with crushed garlic, cumin, and a spoonful of harissa, and bring to a simmer.
Add the cooked chickpeas to the broth and simmer for 10-15 minutes so the flavors meld.
Place torn pieces of day-old bread in the bottom of individual serving bowls.
Ladle the hot chickpea broth and chickpeas over the bread to soften it.
Top each bowl with a poached or soft-boiled egg, a drizzle of olive oil, extra harissa, and capers if using.
Serve immediately with lemon wedges on the side.

title: Chakchouka Tunisienne
instructions: Heat olive oil in a wide skillet and sauté the sliced onion and bell peppers until softened.
Add the garlic and cook briefly until fragrant.
Stir in the chopped tomatoes, tomato paste, harissa, cumin, salt, and pepper, and simmer until the mixture thickens into a sauce, about 15 minutes.
Make small wells in the sauce with a spoon and crack the eggs directly into the wells.
Cover the skillet and cook gently until the egg whites are set but yolks remain soft, about 5-7 minutes.
Serve hot directly from the skillet with crusty bread for dipping.

title: Cassava Leaf Stew (Plasas)
ingredients: 2 lbs ground cassava leaves (fresh or frozen, or canned)
1 lb beef chunks, cut for stewing
1/2 lb smoked fish, cleaned and deboned
2 scotch bonnet peppers, whole or minced
instructions: Season the beef chunks with salt, seasoning cube, and half the chopped onion, then boil in water or stock until tender, about 40 minutes, reserving the cooking liquid.
If using fresh cassava leaves, wash thoroughly and pound or grind them until finely broken down; if using frozen or canned, drain well.
Heat the palm oil in a large heavy pot over medium heat until it becomes fragrant.
Add the remaining chopped onion and garlic and fry until softened.
Add the smoked fish, dried fish, and scotch bonnet peppers, and stir to combine.
Add the ground cassava leaves and the boiled beef along with its cooking liquid, stirring well.
Cover and simmer over low heat for 45 minutes to 1 hour, stirring occasionally, until the oil rises to the top and the stew thickens.
Season with crayfish and salt to taste, then serve hot over boiled rice.

title: Groundnut Soup (Sierra Leone Style)
ingredients: 1 lb goat meat or chicken, cut into pieces
instructions: Season the goat meat or chicken with salt, seasoning cube, and half the onion, then boil until tender, reserving the stock.
In a bowl, dissolve the groundnut paste in a cup of warm water or stock until smooth and pourable.
In a large pot, heat a little oil and fry the remaining onion, tomatoes, and tomato paste until it forms a thick base.
Add the boiled meat with its stock, then stir in the dissolved groundnut paste.
Add the scotch bonnet peppers and smoked fish, and bring to a gentle simmer, stirring frequently to prevent the groundnut from sticking or burning.
Add the sweet potato if using, and simmer for 25 to 30 minutes until the soup thickens and the oil from the groundnuts rises to the surface.
Season with salt to taste and serve hot with boiled rice.

title: Sierra Leonean Jollof Rice
instructions: Season the chicken with salt, one seasoning cube, curry powder, and thyme, then fry or grill until browned and set aside.
In a large pot, heat the oil and fry the chopped onion until translucent.
Add the blended tomatoes, tomato paste, and scotch bonnet pepper, and fry the mixture over medium heat until the raw tomato smell is gone and the oil separates on top.
Pour in the chicken stock, add the remaining seasoning cube, and bring to a boil.
Wash the rice and add it to the pot, stirring to combine with the sauce.
Cover tightly and cook over low heat, stirring occasionally, until the rice is tender and has absorbed the liquid, about 30 to 35 minutes.
Fluff the rice, top with the fried chicken, and serve.

title: Akara (Bean Cakes)
ingredients: 2 cups black-eyed peas, soaked and peeled
instructions: Soak the black-eyed peas in water for at least 2 hours, then rub off the skins and rinse until the beans are clean and white.
Blend the peeled beans with the onion and scotch bonnet pepper, adding only a small amount of water to form a thick, smooth batter.
Whisk the batter vigorously by hand for several minutes to incorporate air and lighten the texture.
Season the batter with salt just before frying.
Heat oil in a deep pot until hot, then scoop spoonfuls of the batter and drop them carefully into the oil.
Fry the akara in batches, turning occasionally, until golden brown and cooked through, about 4 to 5 minutes per batch.
Remove and drain on paper towels, then serve hot on their own or with bread.

title: Liberian Jollof Rice
ingredients: 1 lb chicken or beef, cut into pieces
instructions: Season the meat with salt, one seasoning cube, and curry powder, then boil or fry until browned and nearly cooked, reserving any stock.
In a large pot, heat the oil and saute the chopped onion until soft and golden.
Add the blended tomatoes and tomato paste, and fry over medium heat, stirring frequently, until the sauce thickens and the oil rises to the top.
Add the bell pepper, scotch bonnet pepper, and the browned meat, and stir to combine.
Pour in the meat stock and remaining seasoning cube, and bring to a boil.
Add the washed rice, stir well, then cover and reduce heat to low.
Cook, stirring occasionally, until the rice is tender and all liquid is absorbed, about 30 minutes.
Fluff the rice with a fork before serving.

title: Palm Butter Soup
ingredients: 2 cups fresh palm nuts, boiled and pounded, or 1 can palm butter/palm cream concentrate
1 lb beef or goat meat, cut into pieces
2 scotch bonnet peppers, whole or minced
instructions: If using fresh palm nuts, boil until soft, then pound and extract the thick red palm cream by straining with water, discarding the fibers and seeds.
Season the beef or goat meat with salt, onion, and seasoning cube, then boil until tender, reserving the stock.
Pour the extracted palm cream, or canned palm butter concentrate, into a large pot along with the meat stock, stirring to combine.
Add the boiled meat, smoked fish, dried fish, and scotch bonnet peppers.
Bring to a gentle simmer over medium-low heat, stirring frequently to prevent sticking, until the oil separates and rises to the top, about 30 to 40 minutes.
Season with salt to taste and continue simmering until the soup reaches a thick, rich consistency.
Serve hot over rice.

title: Liberian Cassava Leaf
ingredients: 2 lbs ground cassava leaves (fresh, frozen, or canned)
instructions: Boil the beef with a portion of the chopped onion, seasoning cube, and salt until tender, reserving the cooking liquid.
If using fresh cassava leaves, wash and pound or finely grind them; if frozen or canned, drain excess liquid.
Heat the palm oil in a large pot until hot, then add the remaining onion and fry until soft.
Stir in the ground cassava leaves, dried shrimp, and scotch bonnet peppers.
Add the boiled beef and its reserved stock, stirring to combine everything evenly.
Add the smoked fish and simmer uncovered over low heat for 45 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the stew thickens and the oil rises to the top.
Adjust seasoning with salt and serve hot over rice.

title: Potato Greens (Liberian Sweet Potato Leaves Stew)
ingredients: 2 lbs sweet potato leaves, washed and finely chopped or ground
1 lb beef or chicken, cut into pieces
instructions: Boil the beef or chicken with half the onion, seasoning cube, and salt until tender, reserving the stock.
Wash the sweet potato leaves thoroughly, then finely chop or grind them.
Heat the palm oil in a large pot and fry the remaining onion until softened.
Add the ground sweet potato leaves and stir well to coat with the oil.
Add the boiled meat with its reserved stock, the smoked fish, and scotch bonnet peppers.
Simmer over medium-low heat for 30 to 40 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the leaves are tender and the stew thickens.
Season with salt to taste and serve hot with rice or fufu.

title: Riz Gras (Guinean Jollof-Style Rice)
instructions: Season the beef with salt and one seasoning cube, then brown it in the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Add the chopped onion and continue to fry until softened.
Stir in the tomatoes and tomato paste, cooking until the mixture thickens and darkens slightly.
Add the carrot, cabbage, scotch bonnet pepper, remaining seasoning cube, and water or stock, then bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer until the beef is tender and the vegetables are cooked, about 30 minutes.
Remove the vegetables and beef and set aside, then add the washed rice to the remaining sauce in the pot.
Cover and cook the rice over low heat until tender and the liquid is absorbed, about 25 to 30 minutes.
Serve the rice topped with the reserved beef and vegetables.

title: Foutou with Peanut Sauce (Guinea)
ingredients: 1 lb plantains, peeled (optional, for mixed foutou)
1 lb chicken or beef, cut into pieces
instructions: Boil the peeled cassava, and plantains if using, in water until very soft.
Pound the boiled cassava and plantains together in a mortar with a pestle, adding a little of the cooking water, until smooth, stretchy, and free of lumps.
Shape the pounded foutou into rounded balls and keep warm.
Season the chicken or beef with salt and seasoning cube, then boil until tender, reserving the stock.
In a pot, fry the onion and tomatoes until softened, then dissolve the peanut paste in a portion of the reserved stock and add it to the pot.
Add the boiled meat and scotch bonnet pepper, then simmer over low heat, stirring frequently, until the sauce thickens and the oil rises to the surface, about 20 to 25 minutes.
Serve the foutou balls alongside the hot peanut sauce.

title: Maafe (Guinean Peanut Stew)
ingredients: 1 lb beef or lamb, cut into chunks
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot and brown the beef or lamb chunks over medium-high heat.
Add the chopped onion and cook until softened.
Stir in the tomatoes and tomato paste, cooking for a few minutes until they break down.
Dissolve the peanut paste in a cup of warm water or stock until smooth, then add it to the pot along with the remaining stock.
Add the scotch bonnet pepper, seasoning cube, carrots, and sweet potato.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer, stirring occasionally to prevent the peanut sauce from sticking, until the meat is tender and the stew has thickened, about 45 minutes to 1 hour.
Adjust seasoning with salt and serve hot over rice.

title: Bobotie
ingredients: 1 kg minced beef (or half beef, half lamb)
2 slices white bread, soaked in 250 ml milk
instructions: Preheat the oven to 160°C (325°F) and grease a medium baking dish.
Fry the onions in a little oil until soft and translucent.
Add the curry powder and cook for a minute until fragrant, then add the mince and brown well, breaking up any lumps.
Squeeze the milk from the soaked bread, mash the bread and stir it into the mince along with the jam, vinegar and raisins.
Season with salt and pepper, simmer for 10 minutes, then spoon the mixture into the baking dish and press flat.
Push the bay or lemon leaves into the top of the mince so they stand upright.
Whisk the eggs with the 125 ml milk and a pinch of salt, then pour evenly over the mince.
Bake for 35–40 minutes until the egg topping is set and golden, then serve with yellow rice and chutney.

title: Biltong
ingredients: 1.5 kg beef silverside or eye of round, cut into long strips along the grain
30 g coriander seeds, toasted and crushed
instructions: Trim any excess sinew from the beef strips, keeping the strips about 3 cm thick.
Dip each strip briefly in the vinegar, then lay the meat out and rub the salt over both sides; let it sit for about an hour.
Rinse off the excess salt quickly with a little more vinegar and pat dry.
Mix the crushed coriander seeds, black pepper, bicarbonate of soda and sugar, then rub this spice mixture generously over all sides of the meat.
Hang the strips on biltong hooks in a well-ventilated, dry, cool space or a dedicated biltong box with airflow, making sure strips do not touch each other.
Dry for 4–7 days depending on humidity and desired texture, checking daily, until the outside is firm and the inside is still slightly pliable (or fully dry for hard biltong).
Slice thinly against or along the grain to serve.

title: Boerewors
ingredients: 200 g pork fat or fatty pork, coarsely minced
1 tablespoon coriander seeds, toasted and crushed
60 ml brown vinegar or red wine vinegar
Natural sausage casings, soaked and rinsed
instructions: Combine the minced beef and pork fat in a large bowl.
Add the crushed coriander, black pepper, cloves, nutmeg and salt, then mix in the vinegar.
Knead the mixture thoroughly by hand until well combined and slightly sticky.
Thread the soaked casing onto a sausage funnel and stuff the meat mixture in firmly, avoiding air pockets, forming one long coil rather than tying into links.
Twist or coil the sausage and refrigerate for at least an hour to firm up.
Braai (grill) the boerewors over medium coals, turning occasionally, for about 15–20 minutes until cooked through and browned, taking care not to pierce the casing.
Serve hot off the braai, often with pap or in a roll.

title: Chakalaka
ingredients: 1 tin (410 g) baked beans in tomato sauce
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot and fry the onion and garlic until soft.
Add the bell pepper and chillies and cook for a few minutes until slightly softened.
Stir in the curry powder and paprika and cook for a minute until fragrant.
Add the grated carrots and chopped tomatoes and simmer for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in the baked beans and simmer for a further 10–15 minutes until the vegetables are tender but still have some bite.
Season with salt to taste and serve warm or at room temperature alongside pap, boerewors or bread.

title: Bunny Chow
ingredients: 1 whole small unsliced white loaf, or 4 quarter loaves
600 g mutton or chicken, cut into pieces
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot and fry the onions until golden.
Add the garlic and ginger and cook for a minute, then stir in the curry powder and cook until fragrant.
Add the meat and brown on all sides, then stir in the chopped tomatoes.
Add enough water to cover, cover the pot and simmer for 40–60 minutes until the meat is tender, adding the potatoes halfway through.
Season with salt and simmer until the curry is thick, with most of the liquid absorbed.
Cut the top off the small loaf and hollow out some of the bread from the centre, keeping the removed bread as 'padkos' (dipping bread).
Spoon the hot curry into the hollowed loaf, garnish with coriander, and serve with the reserved bread piece for scooping.

title: Pap en Vleis
ingredients: Chakalaka or tomato and onion gravy, to serve
instructions: Bring the water to a boil in a heavy pot with a teaspoon of salt.
Slowly sprinkle in the maize meal while stirring continuously to avoid lumps.
Reduce the heat to low, cover, and let the pap cook for 25–30 minutes, stirring every few minutes and adding a splash of water if it becomes too thick.
While the pap cooks, heat the oil in a pan and fry the onion until soft, then set aside.
Season the boerewors or steak with salt and braai or pan-fry over medium-high heat until cooked to preference, turning occasionally.
Simmer the fried onion with chopped tomatoes to make a simple gravy, seasoning to taste.
Stir the pap well until smooth and stiff, then serve alongside the grilled meat and tomato-onion gravy or chakalaka.

title: Potjiekos
ingredients: 1 kg stewing beef or lamb, cubed
instructions: Build a wood or charcoal fire and let it burn down to hot coals, then place the three-legged cast-iron potjie pot over the coals.
Heat the oil in the pot and brown the meat in batches, then remove and set aside.
Fry the onions and garlic in the same pot until softened.
Layer the meat back into the pot followed by the carrots, potatoes and butternut without stirring the layers together.
Pour in the stock, add the bay leaves and thyme, season with salt and pepper, and cover with the lid.
Simmer gently over low coals for 3–4 hours without stirring, occasionally checking and adjusting the coals to maintain a steady, low simmer.
Once the meat is tender and vegetables cooked through, serve directly from the pot with pap or crusty bread.

title: Sadza ne Muriwo
ingredients: 500 g leafy greens (covo, collard greens or spinach), chopped
2 tablespoons peanut butter (optional, for muriwo unyevheri)
instructions: Bring half the water to a boil in a heavy pot, then mix the remaining cold water with the maize meal to form a thin paste.
Stir the maize paste into the boiling water and cook, stirring continuously, until it thickens into a thin porridge.
Gradually add more dry maize meal, stirring vigorously with a wooden spoon (mupunda) after each addition, until the sadza becomes thick and stiff.
Cover and let the sadza steam-cook on low heat for 5–10 minutes, then turn out onto a plate or board and shape into a mound.
For the muriwo, heat the oil in a separate pot and fry the onion until soft, then add the tomatoes and cook until pulpy.
Add the chopped greens and cook until wilted and tender, stirring in the peanut butter if using, and season with salt.
Serve the sadza alongside the muriwo, eaten by hand, pinching off pieces of sadza to scoop the greens.

title: Mopane Worms with Peanut Sauce
ingredients: 1 litre water for soaking and boiling
instructions: Soak the dried mopane worms in warm water for about 20–30 minutes to soften and rehydrate them.
Drain and rinse the worms thoroughly, removing any grit or hard bits.
Boil the worms in fresh water for about 15 minutes until tender, then drain well.
Heat the oil in a pan and fry the onion and garlic until soft and golden.
Add the chopped tomatoes and chilli and cook until the tomatoes break down into a sauce.
Stir in the peanut butter and a little water to loosen it, mixing until smooth.
Add the boiled mopane worms to the sauce, season with salt, and simmer for 10 minutes until well coated and heated through.
Serve hot with sadza.

title: Nyama ne Sadza
instructions: Place the beef chunks in a pot with enough water to cover, add a pinch of salt, and simmer for about 45–60 minutes until tender, skimming off any foam.
Drain the beef, reserving some of the cooking liquid, and set aside.
Heat the oil in a separate pan and fry the onion and garlic until soft.
Add the tomatoes and cook until they break down into a thick sauce, then stir in the crumbled stock cube.
Return the beef to the pan, add a splash of the reserved cooking liquid, and simmer for 15–20 minutes until the meat is well coated and the sauce has thickened.
Meanwhile, prepare the sadza by boiling water, stirring in maize meal gradually, and beating vigorously until thick and smooth, following the standard method.
Season the meat stew with salt and pepper to taste and serve hot alongside the sadza.

title: Galinha à Zambeziana (Piri Piri Chicken)
ingredients: 1 whole chicken (about 1.5 kg), spatchcocked or cut into pieces
6 fresh piri piri (African bird's eye) chillies, or 3 tablespoons piri piri sauce
instructions: Blend the piri piri chillies, garlic, lemon juice, olive oil, paprika, bay leaf and salt into a smooth marinade.
Rub the marinade generously all over the chicken, working it under the skin where possible.
Cover and marinate in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours, preferably overnight.
Preheat a grill or braai to medium-high heat.
Grill the chicken skin-side down first, turning occasionally and basting with the reserved marinade, for about 35–45 minutes until cooked through and charred in spots.
Baste with any remaining piri piri sauce during the last few minutes of grilling for extra heat and flavour.
Rest for a few minutes before serving with rice or xima and a side salad.

title: Matapa
ingredients: 500 g cassava leaves, finely chopped (or fresh spinach as substitute)
200 g small shrimp or crab meat
1 tablespoon palm oil or vegetable oil
instructions: If using fresh cassava leaves, pound them lightly to break down the fibres, then rinse well.
Place the chopped cassava leaves in a pot with a little water and simmer for about 20–30 minutes until tender.
In a separate pan, heat the oil and fry the onion and garlic until softened.
Add the cooked cassava leaves to the onion mixture along with the ground peanuts, stirring to combine.
Pour in the coconut milk and simmer gently for 10–15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the shrimp or crab meat and continue to simmer for another 10 minutes until the seafood is cooked through.
Season with salt to taste and serve hot with xima or rice.

title: Xima com Peixe
ingredients: 300 g white maize meal (or cassava flour, for xima)
4 whole small fish (such as tilapia), cleaned
instructions: Season the cleaned fish with salt, pepper and lemon juice and set aside to marinate briefly.
Heat the oil in a large pan and fry the fish on both sides until golden and cooked through, then remove and set aside.
In the same pan, fry the onion and garlic until soft, then add the chopped tomatoes and simmer into a light sauce, seasoning to taste.
Return the fried fish to the pan and simmer gently in the tomato sauce for a few minutes to absorb the flavours.
To make the xima, bring the water to a boil with the salt, then gradually stir in the maize meal.
Keep stirring vigorously, adding more meal as needed, until the mixture thickens into a firm, smooth dough-like consistency.
Cover and cook on low heat for a few more minutes, then shape into a mound and serve alongside the fish and tomato sauce.

title: Nshima with Kapenta
instructions: Rinse the dried kapenta in warm water to remove excess salt and grit, then soak for about 10 minutes and drain.
Heat the oil in a pan and fry the onion until soft and golden.
Add the tomatoes and chilli and cook until the tomatoes break down into a sauce.
Add the kapenta to the sauce and simmer for about 10–15 minutes until the fish is tender and flavours have combined, seasoning with salt.
To prepare the nshima, bring the water to a boil, mix a portion of the maize meal with cold water to form a paste, and stir it into the boiling water.
Cook, stirring, until it thickens slightly, then add the remaining dry maize meal gradually, stirring vigorously until thick and smooth.
Cover and let steam on low heat for a few minutes, then shape into a mound and serve with the kapenta relish.

title: Ifisashi
ingredients: 500 g mixed leafy greens (pumpkin leaves, sweet potato leaves or collard greens), chopped
100 g raw peanuts, ground into a paste
instructions: Wash and chop the leafy greens, discarding any tough stems.
Heat the oil in a pot and fry the onion and garlic until softened.
Add the chopped tomatoes and cook until they break down into a soft sauce.
Stir in the ground peanut paste along with the water, mixing until smooth and well combined.
Add the chopped greens to the pot and stir to coat them in the peanut sauce.
Cover and simmer gently for 15–20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the greens are tender and the sauce has thickened.
Season with salt to taste and serve hot with nshima.
